question: Do independently constructed division-polynomial x-maps for [N] have exact degrees (N^2,N^2-1), agree with direct scalar multiplication on every point of the frozen extension panel, and exhibit the predicted denominator-degree collapse for the excluded characteristic scalar [p]?
positive_checks: the [N] numerator and denominator have exact degrees N^2 and N^2-1
their leading coefficients are 1 and N^2 mod p
the rational x-map equals the x-coordinate of direct [N]P for every finite non-kernel point
the denominator vanishes at every finite point sent to infinity and nowhere among regular points
the numerator and denominator have no common observed root
controls: adding one to the numerator constant produces at least one regular-point mismatch in every cell
constructing the [p] denominator in characteristic p yields degree strictly below p^2-1 in every base-curve family
the excluded [p] leading coefficient at expected degree p^2-1 is zero
measurements: exact polynomial degrees and leading coefficients
complete affine-point, regular-point, pole-point, map-failure, pole-failure, cancellation, and mutation-failure counts
division-polynomial base-field operation counts and direct-evaluation extension-field/group operation counts

producer.method: division-polynomial recurrence over F_p plus exhaustive evaluation through the shared extension-field implementation

independent_verifier.method: separate Python prime-extension arithmetic, division-polynomial recurrence, and exhaustive point-action replay

acceptance.primary: all exact degree, leading-coefficient, pointwise-map and pole checks pass in all eight cells; both controls reject in every cell; producer exact fields equal independent replay
acceptance.failure_policy: retain all rows and report failures without changing cells, scalars, controls, or acceptance criteria

claim_boundary: This experiment checks a scalar coordinate-map certificate on three toy prime-field curves. It does not identify the coordinate map with a scheme morphism in Lean, prove its function-field degree, prove duality of V-1 and pi-1, solve ECDLP, or establish subexponential runtime.
